record.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
record.scope: The units in appliesTo declare RECOVER in this production reference. The strategy is shared; differences are star count, max HP, range and passive.
record.summary: The caster heals itself by 25 / 25 / 50 / 100 percent of its CURRENT max HP (fallback 100) through handleHeal(request, self, apBoost 1, crit); it needs no target. handleHeal checks wound FIRST: a wounded caster heals 0 but, under BLOODMOON weather with BLOOD_STONE items, requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the raw request), apBoost 1, crit) instead (the shield helpers then apply Belt, AP, crit, enrage, alive gate; Protect does not stop it). Otherwise, at hp > 0 and without Protect: AP, crit, x1.3 BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED, x0.5 burn, x0.5 enraged, x1.2 ZENITH, rounded, capped at missing HP; overheal with the GRASS effect requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal). No damage, status or movement.

targeting.note: requiresTarget = false, so the cast does not need a target in range; the cast target is not used.

declaredRaw.label: requested heal = percent of the caster's current max HP

effects.scaling: requested = percent/100 x pokemon.maxHP; then AP: x(1 + AP/100) because apBoost is 1; then x critPower only if the cast rolled a crit (canCritByDefault false, so this needs ABILITY_CRIT)
effects.resolution: applied: the wound check comes FIRST: a wounded caster (status.wound) gets 0 healing and, with BLOODMOON weather and BLOOD_STONE items, a requested addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the raw request), apBoost 1, crit) that the shield helpers scale (Big Eater Belt, AP, crit, enraged x0.5) and refuse at 0 hp (Protect does not stop it; see core-mechanics section J); otherwise 0 at 0 hp or with status.protect (Rune Protect alone blocks nothing); then x1.3 BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED, x0.5 burn, x0.5 enraged, x1.2 ZENITH, rounded, capped at missing HP. The uncapped excess (overheal, from the rounded heal) requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal, itself, 0, false, false) if the caster has the GRASS synergy effect. Requested, applied (healReceived) and overheal are separate amounts; the strategy ignores the returned values.

starBehavior.note: indexed by the casting entity's stars; 1 and 2 stars heal the same 25 %; the 4-star entry (100 %, also the fallback) are declared in the tables but unused by the bound baseline classes. maxPP, range and max HP are in appliesTo / the unit blocks.

record.positionalConditions: None: the strategy reads no coordinates.
record.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state or modes. Each cast spends maxPP of PP and heals once; healing is capped by missing HP, so a cast at full HP produces only overheal.
record.rawVsResolved: Requested: 25 % (1 and 2 stars), 50 % (3 stars) or 100 % (4 stars / fallback) of the caster's current max HP, x(1 + AP/100) [x critPower if the cast crit] inside handleHeal. Applied: after the wound branch, the heal helper's reductions and multipliers and the cap at missing HP; the applied amount can be 0 (wound, protect) and never exceeds missing HP; a wounded caster may instead get a requested Blood Moon shield.

Evidence: source reading, mechanical checks and executed probes. The pinned helper text (handleHeal, addShield, addMaxHP, the Belt / Twist helpers) and the real RecoverStrategy strategy text were run against stand-in units with controlled callbacks (probes/pinned-helper-probe.mjs, section CATCHUP_D1); the whole ability in a real fight, targeting and timing before the cast, and full battles were NOT executed, and nothing was observed in a live game. Executed (maxHP 1000, hp 500): requests 250 / 500 / 1000, AP / crit, protect, Rune Protect, burn, ZENITH, the wound branch with the Blood Moon shield request, and the Grass overheal request.
